author: blu
body: The Network effect is the right to talk to the network, and the rows a program declares to earn it: Network.Read to receive, Network.Write to send. The NIC intrinsics carry these rows, and so does everything built over them.

author: blu
body: The operations that use it live in Net chapter HttpFetch -- fetch, post and resolve-dns. They are not declared here, and that is deliberate. They were, once: three effect operations with no handler anywhere in the tree, so a call to fetch type-checked clean and then died at the very end of emit with CDX2040, an unresolved call. The type checker vouched for a name the compiler could not keep. An implementation needs NetIO, NetIO is codex.os, and a foreword chapter may not depend on codex.os -- so the honest place for them is not here. A chapter that wants them cites Net chapter HttpFetch and gets definitions that do the thing. A chapter that does not gets CDX3002 on the name, at the first opportunity, which is the truth: it asked for something it did not bring.
